source_findings.finding: NativeCleared sets a Dedicated server READY only when last_heartbeat_at is newer than the server freshness window, token_revoked_at is NULL, and token_expires_at is future; otherwise it deliberately sets UNHEALTHY.
A fresh server heartbeat requires a real gst_ credential, valid state transition, and capability fields; matchlobby AuthorityHeartbeat does not update game_servers.last_heartbeat_at.
The real server credential is a random gst_ token whose SHA-256 is persisted; a stale or synthetic hash cannot authenticate a heartbeat.
The private fixture inserts a READY row with server_token_hash=SHA256(serverID) and prepare-time last_heartbeat_at; it does not create or retain a valid gst_ registration credential.
The cleanup driver performs service calls and exact supervisor receipt checks; it does not write SQL state directly. Its READY assertion correctly exposed the fixture's missing fresh heartbeat.

The canonical service routes issue registration credentials through the authenticated player/admin path, register game servers at POST /v1/game-servers, and protect heartbeat plus match-attempt operations with credential proof. AuthorityHeartbeat is a separate match lease signal.

Registration returns the runtime server token and node certificate only after the registration credential is redeemed; heartbeat requires the bearer runtime token and signed request proof, with native admission fields carried in the heartbeat body.

The documented production flow is a one-time instance-bound registration credential issued through the Control Plane and consumed by the Toolbox registration worker. It forbids putting the credential in Payload, command lines, or logs; the legacy environment-token path is not the canonical wrapper flow.

canonical_flow: authenticated verified player or authorized administrator issues an instance-bound registration credential
Toolbox registration worker redeems it at POST /v1/game-servers
the worker keeps the returned gst_ runtime token and node certificate private
the worker sends signed POST /v1/game-servers/{server_id}/heartbeat requests with the exact current capability fields

registration_path_review.blocking_classification: The 74000 reuse attempt is blocked by an unexecuted authorized registration/heartbeat prerequisite, not by a proven backend defect. It must be retried only through the canonical service flow when the isolated test has an authorized verified identity or administrator approval; no handwritten token, SQL READY write, or synthetic capability bit is valid evidence.

conclusion.blocking_guard: No valid game-server registration credential/heartbeat exists for the private inserted server row; the service therefore refuses to return it to READY after NativeCleared. The guard is expected safety behavior.
